stories.headline: Franco-Ukrainian AI air-defense startup Alta Ares raises €50M Series A to scale drone interceptors

key_facts.fact: Alta Ares raised a €50M Series A led by Air Street Capital, with Cherry Ventures, OTB Ventures and Harpoon Ventures participating.

The startup, founded in 2024, builds AI-powered systems to detect, identify and intercept enemy drones and missiles, and says its products are already deployed in active conflict zones in Europe and the Middle East.
Co-founder and CEO Hadrien Canter says three teams are working with militaries in three conflict zones where Alta Ares systems are currently intercepting targets.
Alta Ares operates two interceptor classes: a short-range system aimed at Iranian Shahed-style drones and a medium-range interceptor for cruise missiles and glide bombs.
The €50M will be used mainly to scale production, plus hiring and international expansion across France and Ukraine.

Alta Ares' product stack includes Pixel Lock for embedded detection and tracking, Gamma for autonomous interceptor guidance, X-Lock for short-range drone interception and Black Bird for faster aerial threats; in early 2026 it tested Black Bird at -25°C in Estonia, reaching 450 km/h.

stories.headline: Amazon signs multibillion-dollar Corning fiber deal to wire US AI data centers, adding 1,000 jobs

key_facts.fact: Amazon announced a multiyear, multibillion-dollar agreement with Corning to supply optical fiber, cable and connectivity for its expanding US data center infrastructure.
The deal creates 1,000 new advanced manufacturing jobs at Corning's North Carolina facilities, plus hundreds of construction jobs to expand those plants.
Corning shares rose roughly 7-8% on the announcement; the company's stock has more than doubled in 2026 and is up nearly sixfold since end-2023.
The Amazon agreement follows up to $6B from Meta in January and up to $3.2B from Nvidia in May, the latter to build three Corning plants dedicated to the chipmaker.
Corning has previously announced plans to increase US-based optical connectivity manufacturing capacity tenfold and expand domestic fiber production capacity by more than 50%.
Amazon is spending roughly $200B on AI data center infrastructure this year and has committed $10B to North Carolina data centers alone.

stories.headline: Anthropic says Claude Mythos Preview turns disclosed vulnerabilities into working exploits in hours, not weeks

key_facts.fact: Anthropic researchers ran Claude Mythos Preview against 18 Firefox security patches and got 8 working code-execution exploits, with the first exploit produced in under an hour of Mozilla releasing the patch.

On 21 Windows kernel patches with no source code available, Mythos Preview produced 18 proof-of-concept crashes (first in 31 minutes, all within six hours) and 8 full exploit chains escalating a low-privilege user to SYSTEM level.
Anthropic estimates the Windows kernel privilege-escalation chains cost roughly $1,700-$2,200 in API credits, averaging about $2,000 per exploit.

Anthropic concludes that publicly available models with safeguards disabled can also build exploits, though fewer than Mythos Preview, and argues that 'N-day has become dangerously misleading. N-hour is closer to the reality we now operate in.'
For Firefox, the patched stable release was still 18 days away when Mythos Preview produced its first working exploit from the patch diff.

stories.headline: Apple unveils AFM Cloud Pro running on Nvidia Blackwell B200 GPUs inside Google Cloud at WWDC

key_facts.fact: Apple revealed at WWDC that its most powerful new model, Apple Foundation Model Cloud Pro, will run in the cloud on Nvidia GPUs inside Google Cloud, extending Apple's Private Cloud Compute infrastructure.
The cloud tier uses Nvidia Blackwell B200 GPUs and turns on Nvidia's confidential computing feature, which encrypts data while it is being processed on the chip.

AFM Cloud Pro is the only one of Apple's five new foundation models optimized for Nvidia GPUs instead of Apple Silicon, and adds roughly 10% in text response quality, 14% in image understanding and 14% on math tasks over AFM Cloud.

Apple says it routes Siri queries through three tiers: simple tasks on-device, moderate ones to Apple's Private Cloud Compute servers, and the heaviest to Nvidia GPUs in Google Cloud, with requests "never stored" and inaccessible to anyone.
This marks Apple's first use of Nvidia chips in roughly a decade, with training done on Google's cloud TPUs while serving runs on Nvidia GPUs.
Apple's contract reportedly bars Google from training future models on Apple user data, and Apple says Google receives no Apple user data through the arrangement.

stories.headline: Apple unveils Siri AI at WWDC with on-device MoE model and Gemini-powered cloud, delayed in EU and China

key_facts.fact: At WWDC 2026 Apple announced a redesigned Siri built on a new Apple Foundation Models architecture, including a Camera-app Siri mode for visual intelligence and a Dynamic Island-based interface.
Apple's on-device Siri stack uses a 3B dense model plus a roughly 20B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 1-4B active parameters, decided once per prompt by early routing.

Apple Foundation Model Cloud Pro runs on Nvidia GPUs in Private Cloud Compute and is built on Google Gemini foundation models and data, with Apple doing its own pre-training, post-training and RL on top.
Apple says its most powerful on-device AI model requires an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air, an M4-or-later iPad or an M3-or-later Mac, each with at least 12GB of RAM.

Siri AI will not ship in the European Union or China when the new features arrive in beta later this year; Apple blamed the EU's DMA in a full-page press release and addressed the China delay in a footnote.
Apple opened a Foundation Models framework and a new Core AI framework to developers, plus Xcode enhancements aimed at agentic coding workflows.
Apple announced an Apple Intelligence feature that uses agentic AI to automatically change compromised passwords and store them in the Passwords app.

stories.headline: China drafts $295B five-year plan to build nationwide AI data centers with mostly local chips

key_facts.fact: China is drafting plans to spend $295 billion over the next five years building AI data centers nationwide, according to Bloomberg sources.
More than 80% of the technology in the buildout would come from local suppliers including Huawei, as Beijing accelerates its push for AI self-sufficiency.

Separately, a group of Chinese tech companies including Alibaba and memory maker CXMT is launching a roughly $577 million private-equity fund aimed at strengthening China's 'hard tech' sectors amid tightening US export controls.
On the same day, the US Department of Defense added Alibaba, BYD and Baidu to its list of Chinese entities deemed to support the Chinese military.

stories.headline: Cursor hits $4B annualized revenue ahead of expected SpaceX acquisition

key_facts.fact: AI coding startup Cursor passed $4 billion in annualized revenue in the past week, up from $3 billion in April and $2 billion in February, according to a person familiar with the matter.
SpaceX announced in April 2026 an option to acquire Cursor's parent Anysphere for $60 billion later this year, or pay $10 billion as a breakup fee if it walks away.
As part of the April deal, Cursor is using xAI's Colossus supercomputer for training, with compute described as equivalent to roughly one million H100 GPUs.

SpaceX is deferring the full Cursor acquisition until after its imminent IPO, which is targeting a roughly $1.75 trillion valuation; the deal is structured as a call option to avoid disrupting the listing filings.

stories.headline: FDA grants accelerated approval to Boehringer's zongertinib for HER2-mutant non-small cell lung cancer

key_facts.fact: The FDA granted accelerated approval to zongertinib (Hernexeos), made by Boehringer Ingelheim, for adults with unresectable or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC whose tumors carry HER2 (ERBB2) tyrosine kinase domain activating mutations detected by an FDA-authorized test
The decision expands the drug's August 2025 accelerated approval, which had been limited to HER2-mutant NSCLC patients who had already received prior systemic therapy
Regulatory support derived from Beamion LUNG-1 (NCT04886804), a single-arm, open-label, multicenter, multicohort trial of zongertinib in patients with HER2 gene changes
The application was part of the FDA Commissioner's National Priority Review Voucher pilot program, designed to accelerate review of products addressing national priorities

stories.headline: Google orders 3M+ Intel-made TPUs for 2028 as Nvidia tests Intel 18A; Intel jumps 11%

key_facts.fact: Google has placed a firm order with Intel to manufacture more than three million in-house tensor processing units in 2028 after months of testing Intel's packaging technology.
Morgan Stanley estimates Google will produce more than six million TPUs across 2027 and 2028, meaning Intel's order accounts for roughly half of the projected 2028 output.

Nvidia is running early multi-project wafer runs on Intel's 18A process and is testing whether Intel can build a processor that fuses four GPU dies into one, a design tied to Nvidia's next-generation Feynman GPU architecture due in 2028.
SK Hynix is also testing whether its high-bandwidth memory works reliably with Intel's advanced packaging.
Intel shares jumped about 11-12% on the news.

stories.headline: Google upgrades NotebookLM with Gemini 3.5, Antigravity and agentic research capabilities

key_facts.fact: Google announced an update to NotebookLM that moves the research tool to Gemini 3.5 as the default model, adds agentic capabilities and introduces new output formats for multi-step research.
The upgraded NotebookLM also runs on Antigravity and is being rolled out globally on the web starting with Google AI Ultra users and Workspace business customers with AI Ultra or AI Expanded access.
Google also cut the price of its Google AI Plus plan to $4.99/month from $7.99 and doubled included storage to 400GB.

stories.headline: Federal judge in Boston strikes down Trump's $100K H-1B visa fee as an unlawful tax

key_facts.fact: US District Judge Leo Sorokin in Boston vacated Trump's $100,000 fee on new H-1B visa applications, ruling that the policy violated the federal Administrative Procedure Act and the Constitution

Sorokin concluded the payment is functionally a tax that Congress had not delegated to the executive branch, writing 'the substance and application of the $100,000 payment reveal that it is a tax, regardless of what the payment is called'

The ruling came in a lawsuit filed by 20 Democratic state attorneys general; Trump implemented the fee via a presidential proclamation in September, arguing the H-1B program was being misused through 'large-scale replacement of American workers'
The judge cited the Supreme Court's February 2026 ruling striking down Trump's emergency-law tariffs, applying the same logic that the president lacks authority to levy a tax under immigration law
The fee dramatically suppressed demand: as of February 15, US Citizenship and Immigration Services had received just 85 payments of the $100,000 fee, the administration disclosed in March filings
White House spokesperson Taylor Rogers said the administration would appeal, noting that a federal judge in Washington DC had upheld a similar order in December

organizations: U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts

stories.headline: Iceye raises over €1B led by General Atlantic at €10B valuation as defense space demand surges

key_facts.fact: Iceye raised €450 million (USD 520 million) in a primary Series F round led by General Atlantic at a valuation of over €10 billion (over USD 12 billion); with a secondary placement the total transaction exceeds €1 billion
Additional investors include Solidium, Tesi, Varma, Ilmarinen, Lifeline Ventures, Nokia, Qatar Investment Authority (QIA), and TCV
Six months ago, in December 2025, Iceye was valued at €2.4 billion in a €150 million Series E led by General Catalyst, making the new round a more than fourfold valuation jump
The €450 million primary round is one of the largest single venture rounds for a European defence technology company; Iceye operates the world's largest SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) constellation

Iceye started as a climate monitoring business but has grown into a €10 billion company driven by higher defence spending in Europe and the Middle East; Poland recently signed a ~€200 million radar satellite deal, and the company is targeting €1 billion in revenue in 2027

stories.headline: Finnish SAR satellite maker Iceye raises €1B at €10B valuation, quadrupling six-month-old mark

key_facts.fact: Iceye raised €450M ($520M) in a primary Series F round led by General Atlantic at a valuation of over €10B (over $12B); including a secondary placement, the total transaction exceeds €1B.
The €10B valuation is roughly four times the €2.4-2.5B mark set six months ago, when General Catalyst led a €200M round.
New investors include Qatar Investment Authority, TCV and Nokia as a strategic investor, alongside Finnish state funds Solidium, Tesi, Varma and Ilmarinen plus existing backer Lifeline Ventures.
The €450M primary tranche is one of the largest single venture rounds for a European defence technology company.
Iceye operates the world's largest synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite constellation; in 2025 it surpassed €250M in revenue and €100M in EBITDA.
Iceye was founded in Finland in 2014 and now has more than 1,000 employees globally.

stories.headline: Iran and Israel halt strikes at Trump's request after first fire exchange since April truce

key_facts.fact: Iran fired nearly 30 missiles at Israel; Israel struck military sites in Iran, marking the first exchanged strikes since a ceasefire began in early April

Iran's Khatam Al-Anbiya Central Headquarters announced a halt to strikes, framing it as a 'completed operation' delivering a 'painful response' over Israeli strikes on Beirut's Dahiyeh district, while warning of 'far more intense and crushing' retaliation if Israel attacks again

Trump posted on Truth Social that both sides were seeking an immediate ceasefire and said negotiators were in the 'final throes' of a Middle East peace deal; an Israeli official said Israel halted strikes on Iran at Trump's request
Netanyahu said 'fire is on hold' against Iran but warned that if Tehran 'make the mistake of resuming attacks against us, we will respond with full force'

Iran's initial attack on Sunday evening was retaliation for Israeli strikes on Beirut's southern suburbs, which Tehran views as a violation of the US-Iran ceasefire that requires halting hostilities in Lebanon

Despite the pause between Iran and Israel, Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon killed at least 14 people on Monday, according to the Lebanese health ministry; Israel said offensive operations against Hezbollah would continue 'at full force'

stories.headline: Meta launches $115M America's Workforce Academy with job guarantees to staff AI data center buildout

key_facts.fact: Meta is committing $115 million in the first year to America's Workforce Academy, a free skilled-trades training program with a guaranteed job for every graduate.
Meta calls it the largest private-sector commitment to skilled trades training with a job guarantee in US history.

The four- to five-week bootcamp covers power generation, grid modernization and data center construction; pilots launch in Indianapolis, Baton Rouge, Houston and Columbus, with the first cohort in Baton Rouge.
Meta covers tuition, airfare, lodging and pays a daily stipend; graduates earn an NCCER credential plus an America's Workforce Certificate, both portable across employers.
Meta says it expects to extend roughly 3,300 job offers to graduates in the program's first year; partners include Associated Builders and Contractors and CBRE.
The program lands amid a US construction shortage of roughly 349,000 workers this year and follows Meta's recent layoff of 8,000 employees.

organizations: National Center for Construction Education and Research

stories.headline: Meta commits $115M to a free 5-week 'Workforce Academy' that guarantees data center construction jobs

key_facts.fact: Meta is launching a 'Workforce Academy', a $115 million free five-week program to train Americans to build its data centers, with participants guaranteed a job at one of Meta's construction sites
The initiative comes shortly after Meta cut about 8,000 employees and as the company ramps up massive AI data-center construction in the US

The program was announced via a Wall Street Journal op-ed co-authored by former Trump 45 alum Dina Powell McCormick and tradesman advocate Mike Rowe (mikeroweworks), framing it as tech and trades as 'interdependent, not rivals'

stories.headline: NinjaOne hits $12.3B valuation in $400M+ secondary; founders retain control of IT management platform

key_facts.fact: NinjaOne raised more than $400 million in Series C extensions at a $12.3 billion post-money valuation, more than doubling its $5 billion valuation from February 2025

The Series C extension included Wellington Management, Teachers' Venture Growth, BDT & MSD Partners, Sequoia Capital, ICONIQ, Hedosophia, NEA, Washington Harbour Partners, CapitalG and Pinegrove Opportunity Partners
NinjaOne is now one of the most valuable VC-backed cybersecurity companies, surpassing Cyera, according to co-founder Chris Matarese
The company posted ~70% year-over-year growth in 2025, achieved profitability in Q1 2026, and was named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Endpoint Management Tools

NinjaOne remains founder-led and debt-free; co-founders Sal Sferlazza and Chris Matarese remain the largest equity holders and retain majority control of the board and voting power; the company has nearly 40,000 customers including Audi, Birkenstock, Carnival, Deloitte and Hyundai

stories.headline: OpenAI confidentially files S-1 with SEC, joining Anthropic and SpaceX in IPO queue

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced on June 8 that it had recently submitted a confidential S-1 to the SEC and was disclosing the filing because it expected the news to leak.
OpenAI was last valued at more than $850 billion after a $122 billion funding round in March 2026 and had been targeting a potential public debut as soon as Q4 2026.
Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the filing process for OpenAI's potential listing.
The filing comes a week after Anthropic submitted its own confidential S-1 on June 1, having closed a $65 billion round at a $965 billion valuation, and days before SpaceX is set to start trading.

Investor forecasts reviewed by the WSJ suggest OpenAI's pace of cash consumption would be unprecedented among publicly traded companies; OpenAI has also missed some internal revenue targets while Anthropic has pulled ahead among business customers.

stories.headline: Pentagon adds Alibaba, Baidu, BYD, Nio and dozens more to Chinese military companies list

key_facts.fact: On June 8 the US Department of Defense published an updated Section 1260H list designating Alibaba, Baidu, BYD, Nio, WuXi AppTec, Unitree, TP-Link, JA Solar, Trina Solar, CALB, EVE Energy, Hesai, RoboSense, BOE and CATL among more than 60 additions as 'Chinese military companies'

With these additions, the Pentagon has now declared all three of China's top AI champions (Alibaba, Baidu and Tencent) as supporting the People's Liberation Army; Tencent was added in 2025 and has been seeking removal

Starting June 30, 2026, the FY 2024 National Defense Authorization Act will prohibit DoD from entering into or renewing direct contracts with listed entities; indirect-procurement restrictions take effect in 2027

The designation does not impose sanctions or block US trading but creates reputational and supply-chain risk; the list now includes more than 100 businesses, and an earlier version published briefly in February was withdrawn before being formally reissued
Alibaba called the designation baseless and said it would 'take all available legal action'; Baidu 'categorically' rejected the designation and WuXi AppTec called its listing 'incorrect'

The Pentagon's basis for Nio's designation cited direct and indirect SASAC affiliation and classification as a military-civil fusion contributor; for BYD, the basis was that the company operates within a military-civil fusion enterprise zone, without evidence of direct PLA contracting or technology transfer
